transcript:
Advisor: Good morning Walter, it's Sarah. How was your summer?
Walter: Oh, fine, fine. Hot. I've been getting out more, actually. Going to the Tuesday group at church.
Advisor: That's wonderful. So for today, I wanted to review the ladder and talk about a small rebalance in the managed account. Bonds have drifted a bit above target.
Walter: What's my balance right now?
Advisor: The total across your accounts is about $612,000.
Walter: Okay. Okay, good.
Advisor: So the rebalance would trim about $15,000 of the intermediate bond fund back into short-term Treasuries to get you back to your target mix. It keeps you conservative.
Walter: Mm-hm. And sorry, what was the balance again?
Advisor: About $612,000, Walter.
Walter: Right, right. Six twelve. I didn't write it down.
Advisor: No problem. Are you comfortable with the rebalance?
Walter: Yes, go ahead with the rebalance. That's fine. You know, my friend Daniel from church says I'm too conservative. He says bonds are for people who've given up.
Advisor: Daniel? I don't think you've mentioned him before.
Walter: He's new to the group. Very sharp fellow, does something in investments. Anyway, it's just talk.
Advisor: Well, your plan is built around steady income, and that's still working. We can always discuss it.
Walter: Sure. Do the rebalance. And say hi to the office for me.
Advisor: Will do. I'll send a confirmation of the rebalance in writing.
